newsitem.title: UK: Energy bid talks spark other sector shares.
newsitem.headline: Energy bid talks spark other sector shares.

text.p: The former energy unit of industrial conglomerate Hanson Plc is in talks with Oregon utility PacifiCorp, the first U.S. utility to bid for a British power company under the new Labour government.
Energy Group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor, said after the market closed Tuesday that it was in friendly talks with Portland, Ore.-based PacifiCorp on a merger.

It said any offer would be expected to be priced at about a 20 percent premium to its closing share price on Tuesday of 580 pence, which already valued it at around three billion pounds ($4.9 billion).
Energy Group shares surged to 672 pence Wednesday morning but later eased off their highs and were up 70 pence at 650 pence per share by noon.
"The big news is that the Americans are back," said Yamaichi utilities analyst Nigel Hawkins.

But there was scepticism that other bids would follow, as The Energy Group is a unique proposition, with coal interests in the United States through its Peabody coal unit and British power generation and supply businesses.

A possible bid from Atlanta utility Southern Co. for National Power was blocked around a year ago by the former Conservative government, which vetoed any takeover of the privatised generators until supply and generation markets were fully competitive.
Energy Group, split off from Hanson in February, is Britain's fourth-largest generator after it bought 6,000 megaWatts of capacity from National Power and PowerGen to satisfy competition authorities.

Its supply unit, Eastern Electricity, was one of the 12 Regional electric companies set up by the former Conservative government and bought by Hanson in September 1995. It also owns the U.S. coal business Peabody Resources Ltd.
Analysts said there was scant reason on competition or regulatory grounds for the new Labour government to block a takeover.
"I can't see any obvious problems for the government. The Rec has already been taken over so largely it is just a change of ownership rather than structure," one analyst said.
The new Labour government, which took power with a huge majority on May 1, was critical of the former administration's willingness to pass bids for regional electric companies.

A flurry of bids has seen all but Southern Electric of the original regional electric companies snapped up, many by U.S. companies eager to gain experience of operating in a liberalised, regulated market.
